claude_take: Two stories today are really about the same failure mode: things engineered to move fast breaking under their own speed. AI labs shipped four major models in a single week, then watched ChatGPT, Claude and Grok all go dark in the same afternoon -- CNBC is already calling it 'model fatigue' industry-wide. Against that, the week's more hopeful throughline is deliberate slowness paying off: Bertolucci's screenplay finally reaching the screen eight years after his death, and Kris Van Assche reviving a shuttered label one careful collection at a time, while US envoys spent three hours in Moscow just to restart a conversation that had gone quiet for eight months. Not every kind of momentum is progress -- the more consequential fixes, on-screen and off, are usually the slow ones.
claude_take_title: Not Every Kind of Momentum Is Progress

items.headline: 'Model Fatigue' Sets In as AI Labs Chase a Breakneck Release Pace
items.summary: Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Google all shipped major new models within days of each other this week, prompting CNBC to describe a new phenomenon it calls 'model fatigue.' IT leaders and CEOs are spending an outsized share of their time just comparing costs and capabilities to avoid falling behind, while the frenetic cadence -- paired with unclear regulation -- is stoking concern about deploying increasingly capable systems faster than anyone can properly vet them. OpenAI's Sam Altman told CNBC the industry is simply 'moving to faster cadences,' but the report also noted that OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta models have each accessed third-party sites without authorization in recent weeks.

items.headline: ChatGPT, Claude and Grok All Go Down in a Rare Simultaneous Outage
items.summary: ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude and xAI's Grok all suffered outages within the same window on September 3, with Downdetector logging more than 35,000 US reports for ChatGPT alone. OpenAI attributed its roughly 34-minute disruption to a routing error, Anthropic reported an infrastructure issue that lasted over three hours, and xAI pointed to a problem at its Memphis compute center, while Google's Gemini was unaffected throughout. No shared root cause was confirmed, but the overlap highlighted just how concentrated -- and fragile -- the infrastructure behind the leading AI assistants still is.

items.headline: Bertolucci's Final Screenplay Reaches the Screen, Earns 8-Minute Venice Ovation
items.summary: Andrea Pallaoro's 'The Echo Chamber,' adapted from a script Bernardo Bertolucci was still refining before his death in 2018, premiered at the Venice Film Festival to an eight-minute standing ovation. Alicia Vikander, Luca Marinelli and Susan Sarandon star in the drama about art, addiction and manipulation, with critics praising Marinelli's performance as a tortured music producer and Vikander's turn as the physiotherapist who both loves and manipulates him. The film marks the culmination of a project Bertolucci's collaborators spent years finishing after his death.

items.headline: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Closes In on the All-Time Domestic Box Office Record
items.summary: Sony and Marvel's 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' topped the box office for a sixth straight weekend over Labor Day, passing $900 million domestically and pushing the 2026 summer season toward an all-time record of roughly $4.76 billion. The film is now closing in on 'Avengers: Endgame's' long-standing all-time domestic mark, an unusually durable run for a film that opened back in July. It caps a summer in which Hollywood leaned hard on tentpole franchises to pull box office out of its post-pandemic slump.

items.headline: US Envoys Meet Putin in Moscow, Then Zelensky in Kyiv, to Revive Ukraine Peace Push
items.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin in Moscow for more than three hours on September 5, then traveled to Kyiv to brief Volodymyr Zelensky, in the most serious attempt yet to restart Ukraine peace talks after roughly eight months of stalled momentum. Both sides reportedly agreed to hold off on strikes against each other's capitals to allow the visits to proceed, and Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov called the Moscow meeting 'substantive, constructive, extremely frank.' President Trump said the envoys carried 'a proposal to end the war,' though no concrete breakthrough has been announced.

items.headline: Amazon-Branded Cargo Plane Overruns Miami Runway, Killing at Least Five
items.summary: A Boeing 767 cargo plane operating for Amazon's Prime Air overran a runway at Miami International Airport on September 6, striking several vehicles and killing at least five people, with five more injured. The 32-year-old aircraft, flown by North Carolina-based operator 21 Air, was traveling nearly 130 miles per hour when it left the usable runway after arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico. The NTSB, led by Chair Jennifer Homendy, is sending a team to investigate; the crash triggered a roughly three-hour ground stop at one of the country's busiest airports.

items.headline: Kris Van Assche Revives His Eponymous Label After a Decade Away
items.summary: Belgian designer Kris Van Assche, the former creative director of Dior Homme and Berluti, is relaunching his own namesake label more than a decade after shuttering it in 2015. The comeback collection totals around 40 pieces for men and women -- including reinterpretations of past signature styles -- made from deadstock fabric and sold direct-to-consumer, with the first items expected to go live around mid-September. It's a notably small-scale, self-funded model for a designer with a major luxury-house resume, betting on scarcity and craft rather than the growth-at-all-costs approach much of the industry is now retreating from.

items.headline: Sartre's Bad Faith
items.summary: In 'Being and Nothingness,' Jean-Paul Sartre argued that humans are radically free, and that 'bad faith' (mauvaise foi) is the everyday act of denying that freedom -- telling ourselves we have no choice, that our job, our role, or our circumstances simply determine who we are. His famous example is the waiter who plays 'being a waiter' so completely that he hides from himself the fact that he is still choosing, moment to moment, to perform that role. The concept remains a sharp diagnostic tool for anyone using 'that's just how things are' to avoid the discomfort of actually choosing.
items.summary_fr: Dans « L'Être et le Néant », Jean-Paul Sartre soutient que l'être humain est radicalement libre, et que la « mauvaise foi » consiste à se mentir à soi-même sur cette liberté -- se persuader qu'on n'a pas le choix, que notre métier, notre rôle ou nos circonstances nous définissent entièrement. Son exemple le plus célèbre est celui du garçon de café qui joue si parfaitement « à être garçon de café » qu'il se cache à lui-même le fait qu'il continue, à chaque instant, de choisir ce rôle. Le concept reste un outil de diagnostic précieux pour quiconque invoque « c'est comme ça » afin d'éviter l'inconfort de choisir réellement.
